c.tagline: Bolivia's booming tropical lowland hub, ringed by plazas and the gateway to the Jesuit Missions.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis are unmetered - agree the fare before getting in, and use registered radio taxis or apps (Uber is limited here, Yango is common) for safety, especially after dark. Micros (city buses) and trufis (shared taxis on fixed routes) are the cheap local option.

emergency.note: 110 police, 118 ambulance/emergency medical, 119 fire. English-speaking operators are rare, so having Spanish help is useful.

hood_landmark.Equipetrol: Avenida San Martin, Equipetrol, Santa Cruz
hood_landmark.Sirari: Barrio Sirari, Santa Cruz de la Sierra
hood_landmark.Zona Norte: Ventura Mall, Santa Cruz de la Sierra

avoid.reason: Petty crime; caution in the centre and outer rings at night

hood_desc: The historic core around the leafy Plaza 24 de Septiembre and its cathedral, ringed by arcaded colonial streets, museums, markets, and the first of the city's concentric ring roads; the walkable base for first-timers.

Santa Cruz's most modern and upscale district just north of the center, packed with restaurants and cafes along pedestrian Avenida Monsenor Rivero, malls, and the city's liveliest nightlife on Avenida San Martin.
A quiet, leafy upscale residential enclave just beyond Equipetrol, with gated homes, boutique hotels, and easy access to the dining strip; calm but close to the action.
An affluent gated hillside suburb across the Pirai River, with country clubs, eco-resorts, and river views; a tranquil green retreat a short drive from downtown.
The sprawling northern commercial belt along Avenida Banzer and the outer ring roads, home to big shopping malls, chain hotels, and the airport road; convenient for shoppers and business travelers.
lodging: Los Tajibos, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel
Marriott Santa Cruz de la Sierra Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; avoid ice from unknown sources.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver - a micro or trufi ride is about Bs 2-2.50 (~$0.35); there is no smartcard system. Micros run fixed numbered routes across the ring roads, while trufis are shared taxis and minivans on set routes.
transit.hours: Micros and trufis run roughly 6am to 10-11pm; after that, radio taxis and ride apps fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Santa Cruz has no metro or tram. Public transport is entirely road-based: numbered micros (city buses) and trufis (shared taxis on fixed routes), supplemented by taxis and ride-hailing.

train: Estacion Santa Cruz (Ferroviaria Oriental, Terminal Bimodal)

transit.m: Public micro/minibus to city center, ~40 min
Airport taxi to city center, ~25 min

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving ~10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not required.
